To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the borders of cis-regulatory DNA preferentially harbor divergent transcription factor binding motifs in the human genome.
the borders of cis-regulatory elements preferentially harbor the divergent TF binding motifs.
the divergent transcription factor binding motifs tend to be accumulated in the edges of regulatory DNA regions and are associated with genes involved in developmental regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolutionary dynamics of cis-regulatory DNA elements in eukaryotic genomes.
the relationship between the divergence levels of TF DNA-binding motifs and their occurrence at cis-regulatory regions in the human genome.
the evolution of cis-regulatory sequences and the mechanisms of TF binding motif divergence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the divergent binding motifs are more likely to be found in the borders of cis-regulatory DNA sequence, and the genes that neighbor the expanded cis-regulation regions with the most divergence in motifs are associated with the development and morphogenesis.
TF binding motifs are more divergent at the edges of cis regulatory regions than at the core of cis regulatory regions.
cis-regulatory DNA sequence changes and the evolution of TF DNA-binding specificity are not random, but rather occur in a non-uniform manner in the human genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the borders of cis-regulatory DNA elements preferentially accumulate the divergent motifs of TFs in the human genome.

the cis-regulatory elements of the human genome are enriched with the divergent TF binding motifs, which may have been introduced by the expansion of regulatory elements and the accumulation of the divergent TF motifs in the cis-regulatory edges.
the cis-regulatory regions are likely to evolve by the introduction of divergent motifs, and the divergent motifs are preferentially introduced into the borders of cis-regulatory DNA elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cis-regulatory regions of the human genome preferentially accumulate the motifs with the highest levels of evolutionary divergence, and that the genes associated with these regions are enriched in developmental functions.
divergent TF binding motifs are enriched in the edges of the regulatory regions and may be introduced to the cis-regulatory regions during evolution.
the edges of regulatory regions are the most likely places to harbor TFs with divergent DNA-binding specificities.
